# authwise_message (Resource)

A tenant's own wording of one of kit's messages (an invitation, a password reset, a sign-in code), for one `key`, `channel` and `locale`.

**What Terraform applies is published**: there is no draft in configuration, and the plan is the review. The console shows a message set here as set by configuration and opens it read-only. A change made in the console or with awctl all the same shows as drift on the next plan, and apply puts back what is configured.

A message takes exactly one shape:

- `texts`: the named parts of the built-in message (its subject, heading, body, button and so on). A part left out keeps the built-in wording, and the built-in layout renders them, so the brand and spacing stay kit's. A part that differs by case is set per case as `"<part>.<variant>"`.
- `subject`, `html` and `text`: the whole mail.

A value is written in kit's template syntax, `{{ .Recipient.Name }}`; kit refuses a value the message does not offer, and any HTML outside what mail clients allow.

A message laid out in the console's layout editor cannot be written here; managing it replaces the layout.

**Destroying it resets the message to kit's built-in** and drops its published history.

Writing a message needs `identity.messageTemplates.update` at the tenant, which a service account holds through `identity.brandingAdmin`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The invitation's own words: the named parts of the built-in message.
# A part left out keeps kit's wording; kit's layout and the tenant's brand
# render them. A part that differs by case is set per case, such as
# "body.join".
resource "authwise_message" "invitation" {
  key    = "tenant-invitation"
  locale = "en"

  texts = {
    subject  = "Welcome to {{ .Brand.DisplayName }}"
    greeting = "Hello {{ .Recipient.DisplayName }},"
    button   = "Accept the invitation"
  }
}

# The same message in French, written whole.
resource "authwise_message" "invitation_fr" {
  key    = "tenant-invitation"
  locale = "fr"

  subject = "Bienvenue chez {{ .Brand.DisplayName }}"
  html    = file("${path.module}/mail/invitation.fr.html")
  text    = file("${path.module}/mail/invitation.fr.txt")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Which message, as kit names it: `tenant-invitation`, for example. kit lists them, with when each is sent, as message keys. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `locale` (String) The language, as a BCP 47 tag (`en`, `fr-CA`). A tenant may write a locale kit does not ship, which makes the message available in it. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `channel` (String) The channel: `email`, the default and the only one kit renders today. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `html` (String) The whole mail's HTML body. With `subject` and `text`; not with `texts`.
- `managed_by` (String) The mark kit keeps on the message, which has the console show it as set by configuration, read-only: `terraform` by default. Up to 64 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`; name the configuration (`terraform-prod`) when several manage one tenant. Publishing from the console removes the mark, and the next plan puts it back.
- `subject` (String) The whole mail's subject. With `html` and `text`; not with `texts`.
- `tenant_id` (String) The tenant; overrides the provider default. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `text` (String) The whole mail's plain-text body, which mail clients show when they show no HTML. With `subject` and `html`; not with `texts`.
- `texts` (Map of String) The named parts of the built-in message, by part name. A part left out keeps the built-in wording. Not with `subject`, `html` or `text`.

### Read-Only

- `name` (String) The message's full resource name (`tenants/{t}/message-templates/{id}`); serves as the Terraform ID.
- `published_at` (String) When what is live was published, RFC 3339.
- `published_by` (String) Who published what is live.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by key/channel/locale, with the tenant first when it is not the
# provider's default. The message keeps its wording until the next apply.
terraform import authwise_message.invitation tenant-invitation/email/en
terraform import authwise_message.invitation t-01/tenant-invitation/email/en
```
